blind_spots_patched: Chapters 3 and 6 omitted the €538M unprovisioned MLC bundling contingent liability from the Oct 2025 amended complaint, the 26.7% jump in non-cancelable purchase obligations to €1,996M (€4,349M total contractual commitments), the doubling of uncertain tax reserves to €128M, €43M in contested non-income tax assessments, €120M in non-current rights-holder advances, and the €1,121M 9M 2026 OCI markdown on Tencent Music.

The baseline chapters omitted Spotify's EUR/USD currency mismatch (36.0% of 9M 2026 revenue is U.S.-generated while reporting in EUR and executing USD buybacks), the €199M FX drag on 9M 2026 revenue, balance-sheet transaction sensitivity (-€55M USD / -€37M GBP PBT per 10% currency strengthening), and IFRS 18's Jan 2027 reclassification of FX items into Operating Income.

Chapter 3 named the major licensors but omitted exact stream concentration (72% of label-delivered audio streams from UMG, SME, WMG, and Merlin in FY2025), MFN and churn-linked royalty ratchet clauses, and single-source Google Cloud Platform (GCP) lock-in behind €1,996M purchase obligations and +€134M 9M 2026 R&D IT/cloud/AI spend.

Chapter 4 flagged beneficiary certificates qualitatively without quantifying founders' 69.3% combined voting power (Ek 28.8%, Lorentzon 40.5%), the 1.4B authorized beneficiary certificate ceiling without preemptive rights, Heidi O'Neill's Sept 3, 2026 Board resignation, €20M/10% share-price Social Charges volatility, and routine Nov 2026 Rule 10b5-1 Co-CEO option sales.
